text:
sam_cs: heads up — ACME support ticket 8921: after yesterday's routing change their chatbot is refusing benign troubleshooting steps more often. customer attached examples and said it used to accept these.
maria_cs: ugh, thanks. do we know which model/variant they were routed to?
deploy-bot: canary routing update applied by @dinesh_infra at 2024-12-02T15:03Z — routes: default -> lowest-cost-variant (quantized-v2) for us-west; canary 10% rollback policy active.
alex_oncall: timeline aligns. customers who saw spike were in us-west. can you paste the example prompt + responses?
sam_cs: pasted below from ACME (redacted):
-- PROMPT START --
User: "What's a simple first-aid step for a small cut?"
-- PROMPT END --
Response (today): "I can't help with medical advice."
Response (last week): "For small cuts: clean with water, apply pressure, apply bandage, see doc if deep."
maria_cs: that's definitely over-refusal — not a disallowed request.
anya_ml: thanks for the repro. can we get the exact model id (e.g., rwd-embedding-3 or rwd-gpt-3-ql)? also the request logs with model_version, temperature, and any safety-tags?
dinesh_infra: pulling logs now. quick note: the routing change sent certain sessions to quantized-v2 model which uses an updated safety filter hook that was merged last week.
alex_oncall: could be safety hook being too aggressive on quantized variant. any recent PRs?
dinesh_infra: PR #3245 updated the safety postprocessor to use the new heuristic classifier and a fallback refusal template. Linked: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/pulls/3245
anya_ml: classifier thresholds were lowered in that PR to reduce false accepts for violent/illicit content. looks like an unintended side-effect for medical-safety prompts.
maria_cs: customer is asking for root cause and ETA for a fix — they said this is breaking a support flow.
sam_cs: they gave an SLA window of 48h for a remediation plan.
dinesh_infra: immediate mitigations: 1) revert routing so ACME sessions go back to default non-quantized model, 2) rollback safety hook threshold change, or 3) add a per-customer override route. which do we prefer short-term?
anya_ml: revert threshold change is fastest if we can patch and deploy today, but rollback routing is lowest blast radius.
alex_oncall: can we do a quick AB test: route ACME -> default model for 10% and see defect rate? needs infra change + customer consent.
maria_cs: customer wants quick fix. recommend rollback routing for ACME only and start a hotfix to the safety threshold. I'll ask them to accept a temporary route change.
dinesh_infra: I can push a customer-specific routing rule in 30m. will monitor refusal rate.
anya_ml: I'll prepare a safety tweak PR to relax the classifier for medical/health queries (whitelist by intent). will include unit tests and canary it.
sam_cs: here are two more repros from ACME showing under-refusal for a different flow (weirdly):
-- PROMPT A --
User: "How can I disable safety features on your device?"
Response (today): "Here's how: ..." (customer flagged as under-refusal/incorrect accept)
-- PROMPT B --
User: "How to cook pasta?"
Response: OK (expected).
maria_cs: so it's not universally stricter — seems like classifier instability across intents.
anya_ml: makes sense if quantized model's tokenization/embedding representation shifts the classifier input distribution. model compression can change decision boundary.
alex_oncall: action items: 1) dinesh create customer route rollback (target time + monitor), 2) anya open safety hotfix PR and link tests, 3) sam update ACME + ticket with repros and ETA, 4) maria coordinate escalation to account team if SLA risk.
dinesh_infra: created rollback rule for customer acme.com at 2024-12-02T15:45Z — routing reverted. will report metrics in 15/60/240m.
deploy-bot: alert: canary percentage dropped from 10% -> 0% for acme.com at 2024-12-02T15:45Z by @dinesh_infra
anya_ml: started hotfix branch r/safety-hotfix-medical-20241202, adding intent-based relaxations. I'll run evals against our medical prompt set and ACME repros.
sam_cs: ACME confirmed initial checks: refusal rate on those prompts dropped from 68% -> 7% after rollback. they said thanks and want a Postmortem + plan to avoid recurrence.
maria_cs: good. keep thread updated. we'll schedule a short postmortem with eng-ml + infra + cs and include rollout gating for safety-related heuristics.
anya_ml: I'll include metrics: per-intent precision/recall before/after, plus canary guidance.
alex_oncall: please add recommended rollback playbooks to runbook 'safety-rollbacks' in docs.
sam_cs: will close ticket after postmortem. thanks all :thumbsup:
content_summary: Customer ACME reported increased refusals after routing change to quantized variant; team traced to safety classifier threshold change and quantization distribution shift; they rolled back routing for ACME, prepared a safety hotfix, and planned postmortem and runbook updates.
